title: Human-in-the-loop by design: where to put the human in an AI agent
targetKeyword: human in the loop AI design
linkedinPost:
$6.73B — the size of the human-in-the-loop AI market in 2026.

Almost none of that investment goes into the decision that determines whether HITL oversight actually works: where in the workflow the human sits.

Klarna removed humans from their AI customer service process. Quality dropped. They announced a re-hiring initiative. The model performed. The product failed.

Most teams fail in the same three ways:
• They place the human after the decision, not at it
• They give the human output without reasoning — nothing to actually act on
• They make override harder than approve — so the gate becomes rubber-stamp

What I would actually do:
• Map every agent action to the Oversight Calibration Levels (consequence × reversibility) before building
• Design the context package the human receives — reasoning, confidence score, consequence of each choice
• Build the audit trail into the gate at build time, not as a retrofit
• Set a target HITL rate per workflow and review monthly

EU AI Act Article 14 enforcement: August 2, 2026. It requires effective human oversight, not nominal presence.

Revenue per employee increases when humans focus on decisions only humans can make. The gate is where you draw that line — design it deliberately.

Full piece + the Oversight Calibration Levels framework I use to map gate placement — link in comments.

acceptedAnswer.text: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) AI design is the discipline of deciding where in an automated workflow a human must review, approve, or override an AI decision — and designing the interface and context package that makes that intervention meaningful rather than nominal.

mainEntity.name: What does EU AI Act Article 14 require for human oversight of AI systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Article 14 requires that high-risk AI systems include human-machine interface tools enabling effective oversight by qualified natural persons who can interpret AI outputs and intervene, stop, or override the system. Enforcement applies from August 2, 2026. The requirement is for effective oversight — not nominal presence. Auditors will ask whether the gate design could have changed the outcome.

mainEntity.name: How do I decide where to place human gates in an AI agent workflow?

acceptedAnswer.text: Map every consequential action against two variables: consequence severity and reversibility. Use the Oversight Calibration Levels to assign the appropriate gate type. Gate placement is a risk and product decision — not a framework default or an engineering afterthought.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a human gate becomes rubber-stamp approval?

acceptedAnswer.text: The gate becomes a liability launder — the appearance of oversight without its substance. In a regulated context, this creates rather than reduces compliance exposure. If your approval rate at a gate consistently approaches 100%, audit both the gate threshold and the context package the reviewer receives. One or both is misconfigured.
